name: Holmes, the AI Visibility Detective
author: Bonairmedia

sections.description:
One inspector. Three visibility channels. Evidence you can act on.

Holmes, the AI Visibility Detective provides an evidence-based, page-level SEO, AEO, and GEO audit from WordPress. Submit a public URL and optional target query, audience, and conversion goal. The inspector returns three independent channel scores and practical findings that explain the evidence, why it matters, what to change, and how to validate the improvement.

  • SEO: indexability, metadata, structure, links, image accessibility, schema, audience alignment, and conversion alignment.
  • AEO: question coverage, direct answers, FAQs, summaries, lists, tables, and passage structure.
  • GEO: entity identity, authorship, dates, citations, evidence, sameAs connections, schema, and citation context.
  • Built-in inspection: run the page-level audit without an API key.
  • Useful reports: print the results or save them as a PDF from the browser.

The built-in audit works without an external API. When an administrator configures an API key, the submitted URL and optional context are also sent to the configured analysis service. If that service is unavailable, the built-in audit still returns results. Configure your production terms, privacy policy, retention period, and API host before enabling a connected service publicly.

Shortcode

Primary shortcode:

[holmes_ai_visibility_detective]

Example with optional attributes:

[holmes_ai_visibility_detective url="https://example.com" button="Inspect this page"]

The shortcode and saved settings use this Holmes edition’s own identifiers.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the holmes-ai-visibility-detective folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate Holmes, the AI Visibility Detective in WordPress.
  3. Open Settings → Holmes, the AI Visibility Detective to review the button label and optional API settings.
  4. Add [holmes_ai_visibility_detective] to a page or post.
sections.faq:
What makes this inspector different?

It separates SEO, AEO, and GEO into three channel scores, then connects each finding to page evidence, a recommended action, and validation guidance. The built-in audit also works without requiring an external API key.

What does the plugin inspect?

It reviews a public page for page-level SEO, answer-engine optimization (AEO), and generative-engine optimization (GEO) signals.

Does the built-in audit require an external service?

No. The local page audit works without an API key. Administrators can optionally configure a connected analysis service.

What data leaves my site?

With no external API configured, the plugin fetches only the public URL being inspected. When an administrator enables the optional connected service, the submitted URL, target query, audience, and conversion goal may be sent to that service. WordPress passwords and user credentials are not transmitted.

Does it work with every URL?

It works with publicly reachable HTTP or HTTPS pages that return readable HTML. Password-protected pages, private-network addresses, blocked requests, non-HTML files, and content rendered only with JavaScript may not be fully analyzable. The PHP DOM extension is required for the built-in audit.

Can I save the report?

Yes. Use the browser print dialog to print the report or save it as a PDF.

Does this guarantee rankings or AI citations?

No. The plugin identifies page-level signals and improvement opportunities. Search rankings, answer selection, and citations are controlled by third-party systems and cannot be guaranteed.
